info.title: Braiins Hashpower API
info.description:
REST API for applications and account automation integrating with
[Braiins Hashpower](https://hashpower.braiins.com), the SHA-256 hashrate
marketplace.

## Versions

This is transitional version 2. All paths start with `/v2`. Within version
2, changes are backward compatible: new endpoints, new optional request
fields, new response fields and new enum values can appear at any time, so ignore
response fields you do not know and treat unknown enum values as unknown.
Configure generated clients to do the same; some generators reject unknown
enum values by default. Breaking changes would ship as a new major version
under a new path prefix.

The legacy API under `/v1` (API keys in the `apikey` header) is unchanged
and will be retired after a migration period. Those legacy keys are distinct
from Braiins ID API keys and cannot authenticate v2 requests.

## Authentication

Market data and the spot settings are public. Every other endpoint
accepts an OAuth 2.0 access token or a Braiins ID API key, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <credential>`. Browser session cookies are not accepted.
The API is for server-side and native applications: it sends no CORS
headers, so browsers block calls from web pages. This reference is the
exception when it is opened on the API's own host: there it can send test
requests with an API key you enter, which stays in the page.

For OAuth, when a user connects your application, they choose which
Hashpower accounts it may use and approve its scopes:

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `hashpower:read` | Reading accounts, balances, transactions, spot fees, bids, bid hashrate and best shares, and checking pools. |
| `hashpower:write` | Placing, updating and cancelling bids. It does not include `hashpower:read`; request both to manage bids. |

Account owners create API keys on the account page in Braiins ID. A key
acts only on its own account and must have a Hashpower grant. Read operations
require the Viewer or Admin role; placing, updating and cancelling bids
require the Admin role. Keys have roles, not OAuth scopes.

Call `GET /v2/accounts` to list the accounts the credential may act on and use
their `account_id` in every path that contains `{account_id}`. For a key this
is its one account; another account ID, or a key without a resolved default
subaccount, fails with `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED`. OAuth access ends when the user
revokes the connection or loses access to the account. After a key is
revoked or expires, new requests can continue for up to 15 seconds.
Requests already accepted may finish. Keys also require current account
access. No endpoint can withdraw funds.

## Units and formats

- Amounts are integer satoshis (`*_sat`).
- Prices are integer satoshis per EH/day: the price of 1 EH/s of hashrate
  for one day.
- Hashrates are PH/s (`*_ph`). Volumes are EH·day, so price × volume =
  satoshis.
- 64-bit integers are JSON strings, for example `"price_sat": "48500000"`.
  Requests accept numbers or strings.
- Timestamps are RFC 3339 strings in UTC; durations are strings with an
  `s` suffix, for example `"600s"`.
- Field names are snake_case. Enums are strings.
- Responses include every field, with its zero value when it is not set:
  `0` (`"0"` for 64-bit integers), `""`, `false`, `[]` or the enum's
  `*_UNSPECIFIED` value. Fields whose description says when they are
  absent are left out in those cases instead, and so are unset object
  fields such as timestamps.

## Lists

Collections return up to `page_size` items and a `next_page_token`; pass it
as `page_token` to fetch the next page. It is empty on the last page. Time
series take a `limit` instead.

## Retrying changes

`PlaceBid`, `UpdateBid` and `CancelBid` take a client-generated UUID
`request_id`, an idempotency key. Hashpower executes a change at most once
per account (tenant and subaccount) and `request_id`, across credentials
and key rotation, and once it has executed the change, the outcome is final
for that `request_id`: a retry with the same `request_id` and body returns
it, including a rejection. Hashpower keeps each `request_id` and its
outcome for at least 30 days. Reusing a `request_id` with a different body
fails with `REQUEST_ID_REUSED`.

- After a timeout, a 429 or 5xx response, or `OUTCOME_PENDING`, retry with
  the same `request_id` and body.
- After any other error, fix the cause and send the change with a new
  `request_id`. For example, a cancellation refused with
  `CANCEL_GRACE_PERIOD` needs a new `request_id` once the grace period has
  passed.
- If retries still return `OUTCOME_PENDING` after a minute, keep the original request
  record. For an update or cancellation, call `GetBid`. If that read fails, handle the
  read error before deciding to resubmit.

  For an update, compare the fields you requested with the returned bid. If they
  match, no further update is needed. Otherwise, if the update is still intended,
  submit it again with a new `request_id`. Do not replay an outdated update after a
  later change to the bid. The new command is subject to normal validation.

  For a cancellation, do not resend if the bid is `BID_STATE_CANCELING`,
  `BID_STATE_CANCELED`, or `BID_STATE_FULFILLED`. Otherwise, if cancellation is still
  intended, submit it again with a new `request_id`, subject to normal validation.

  For a placement, list all bids with `current_only=false`, including terminal bids.
  Page backward until the results cover the first attempt, allowing for clock skew,
  and compare the placement's terms. A unique memo chosen before the first attempt can
  help correlate a placement, but it is not an idempotency key. A missing match does
  not prove non-execution. Hashpower does not guarantee when a placed bid appears in
  `ListBids`.

  The API does not yet provide conclusive automated placement recovery. Stop automatic
  replacement while the placement's outcome remains unknown. Do not create another
  placement with a new UUID or fall back to v1 solely because the outcome remains
  unknown.

## Rate limits

Requests are limited per client IP address, whether or not they are
authenticated, so all users of a server-side integration share the budgets
of its address. Each endpoint draws from a budget: a burst, refilled at a
steady rate. The endpoint's description states its limit, and its
`x-rate-limit` extension gives the same as data: the `budget`, the `burst`
and the steady rate `per_minute`. Endpoints that name the same budget share
it.

The limits are approximate. Each gateway instance counts them separately,
so `X-RateLimit-Remaining` can differ between consecutive requests. Each
budget also has a ceiling shared by all clients, so under heavy overall
load a request can be limited before its own budget is used up.

A request over the limit fails with HTTP 429 and code 8
(`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`) and is not executed. There is no `Retry-After`
header: retry with backoff, no sooner than `X-RateLimit-Reset` seconds
later. A change can be retried with the same `request_id`. Responses carry
`X-RateLimit-Limit` (the burst), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and
`X-RateLimit-Reset` for the endpoint's budget.

## Errors

Errors use the [`google.rpc.Status`](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors)
format with an HTTP status matching its `code`:

```json
{
  "code": 9,
  "message": "The account's available balance is too low.",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo",
      "reason": "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS",
      "domain": "hashpower.braiins.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

Branch on `ErrorInfo.reason`, never on `message`. Each endpoint lists the
HTTP statuses it returns and the reasons specific to it; all reasons are
listed in the `TradingErrorReason`, `DeliveryErrorReason` and
`PoolErrorReason` schemas. Errors without a reason carry only the status:
malformed requests (400, sometimes with `google.rpc.BadRequest` field
violations) and temporary unavailability (503, retry with backoff). An API
key for another product is rejected with 401 before the endpoint runs,
without an `ErrorInfo.reason`. Hashpower itself can return a JSON
`UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL` error if it could not verify or accept the
request's authentication.

Requests rejected before they reach Hashpower can have a plain-text body;
branch on the HTTP status for those: unknown paths (404), an unknown query
parameter or a body that is not valid JSON for the endpoint (400; unknown
body fields are ignored), a missing, invalid or expired credential or an API
key for another product (401, with
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), and Braiins ID being unavailable to check the
credential (503).

tags.name: AccountService
tags.description:
Accounts available to the caller and their funds.

 An account is a Hashpower account with one bitcoin balance, shared by
 everything the account buys. Every path with `{account_id}`, including the
 spot paths under `/v2/spot/accounts/`, takes the `account_id` returned by
 `ListAccounts`; there is no separate spot account. A token can act only on
 accounts the user granted to the application, while the user still has access.
 A Braiins ID API key acts only on its own account.

 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.

tags.name: BidService
tags.description:
Spot market bids: buying hashrate delivered to your pool.

 A bid buys hashrate at up to `price_sat` per EH/day until its `amount_sat`
 budget is spent or it is cancelled. Delivered hashrate goes to the bid's
 destination pool and worker. Bids are paid from the balance of the account
 in the path, an `account_id` from `ListAccounts`.

 `GetSpotSettings` is public. The other read methods require the
 OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access. Bid changes require
 OAuth `hashpower:write` (which does not imply read) or an API key allowed to
 place, update and cancel bids.

 Each change carries a client-generated `request_id`, its idempotency key,
 scoped to the account across credentials, including API key rotation.
 Once Hashpower has executed a change, the outcome is final for that
 `request_id`: a retry with the same `request_id` and body returns it,
 including a rejection, instead of executing the change again. Hashpower keeps
 each `request_id` and its outcome for at least 30 days. Retry with the
 same `request_id` only after a timeout, a 429 or 5xx response, or
 `OUTCOME_PENDING`. After any other error, fix the cause and send the change
 with a new `request_id`; for example, cancel a bid refused with
 `CANCEL_GRACE_PERIOD` with a new `request_id` once the grace period has
 passed.

 The market applies a placement, update or cancellation when it accepts it,
 and a mutation returns the bid once the bid shows the change, a later change
 that replaced it, or the bid's end. If the bid shows none of these within a
 few seconds, the bid is returned in a transitional state:
 `BID_STATE_CREATING` from `PlaceBid`, `BID_STATE_UPDATING` from `UpdateBid`
 or `BID_STATE_CANCELING` from `CancelBid`. Call `GetBid` until the bid leaves
 that state.

tags.name: DeliveryService
tags.description:
Delivered hashrate over time and best shares attributed to your bids.

 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.
 Hashrates are in PH/s, averaged over each interval.

 Best shares belong to a destination (pool URL and worker), not to one bid. A
 share counts for every bid with that destination from its creation until
 one minute after it ends. Paused periods and bids without purchases are
 included; attribution does not prove that the bid produced the share. Bids
 with the same destination and lifetime show the same best share and count.
 Hashpower records at most one best share per destination
 every 15 seconds, and only one far above the pool's share difficulty, so
 `share_count` counts recorded best shares, not every share delivered. A share
 appears on a bid about 7 minutes after it was found.

tags.name: PoolService
tags.description:
Mining pools used as bid destinations.

 OAuth requires the `hashpower:read` scope; API keys require read access.

tags.name: MarketService
tags.description:
Public market data for the SHA-256 hashrate spot market.

 No authentication is required. Prices are in satoshis per EH/day, volumes in
 EH·day (so price × volume = satoshis), and hashrates in PH/s.

BadRequest.description:
The request is invalid. The endpoint lists its reasons; a malformed
request has none and can carry `google.rpc.BadRequest` field
violations. Unknown query parameters and bodies that are not valid
JSON for the endpoint are rejected before they reach Hashpower, with a
plain-text body.

Conflict.description:
The `request_id` was already used with a different body
(`REQUEST_ID_REUSED`).

Forbidden.description:
The credential may not do this: `UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL` (Hashpower
could not accept the request's authentication), `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`
(OAuth), `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED`, or a reason the endpoint lists.
Bid changes also return `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION` (403) when the key
can read the account but may not change bids.

NotFound.description: The bid does not exist in this account (`BID_NOT_FOUND`).

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Hashpower is temporarily unavailable; retry with backoff. For a change,
`OUTCOME_PENDING` means its outcome is not known: see Retrying changes.
Unavailability detected at the gateway, including Braiins ID being
unable to check the credential, has a plain-text or empty body.

TooManyRequests.description:
The rate limit was exceeded and the request was not executed; retry
later. A change can be retried with the same `request_id`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The burst of the endpoint's budget.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the budget is next refilled.

Unauthorized.description:
The credential is missing, invalid or expired, or the API key is for
another product. The gateway rejects it with a plain-text body and a
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header, without an `ErrorInfo.reason`.
If Hashpower itself answers 401, its JSON body carries
`UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL`.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Bearer` when the gateway rejected the credential.

bid_ids.title: bid_ids
bid_ids.description: Bid identifiers, for example `B1234`: 1 to 100 distinct bids.

bid_best_shares.title: bid_best_shares
bid_best_shares.description: Best shares of the bids that were found, in request order.

missing_bid_ids.title: missing_bid_ids
missing_bid_ids.description:
Requested bids that do not exist in this account, including bids placed
 moments ago.

share_hash.title: share_hash
share_hash.description: Block header hash, lowercase hex, in the byte order block explorers show.

network_difficulty.title: network_difficulty
network_difficulty.description: Network difficulty of the share's job. Absent when unknown.

closeness.title: closeness
closeness.description:
`difficulty` divided by `network_difficulty`; 1 or more would have found
 a block. Absent when the network difficulty is unknown.

time.title: time
time.description: When the share was found, up to about 15 seconds later.

block_height.title: block_height
block_height.description: Height of the block the share's job was for. Absent when unknown.

hashrate_ph.title: hashrate_ph
hashrate_ph.description:
Hashrate the destination accepted from Hashpower, from every bid
 delivering to it, averaged over the clock-aligned 10 minutes before those
 the share was found in. Absent when unknown, and for up to about 15 minutes
 after the share.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BestShare.title: BestShare
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BestShare.description: A best share recorded for a destination.

share_count.title: share_count
share_count.description:
Best shares attributed by destination and bid lifetime, including paused
 periods and the one-minute grace period after the bid ends.

best_share.title: best_share
best_share.description: The best share with the highest difficulty. Absent until one is recorded.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BidBestSha.title: BidBestShare
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BidBestSha.description: A bid's best share and how many best shares count for it.

samples.title: samples
samples.description:
Samples, oldest first, from the bid's first to its last interval with
 delivery.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BidHashrat.title: BidHashrate
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.BidHashrat.description: A bid's delivered hashrate, one sample per interval.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.DeliveryEr.title: DeliveryErrorReason
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.DeliveryEr.description:
Values of `google.rpc.ErrorInfo.reason` returned by `DeliveryService`. The
 error domain is `hashpower.braiins.com`. New reasons may be added; handle
 unknown reasons by their gRPC/HTTP status.

 - `UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL` (401/403): Hashpower could not verify or accept
   the request's authentication. Invalid API keys and keys for another product
   are rejected with HTTP 401 at the gateway, without an `ErrorInfo.reason`.
 - `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` (403): The OAuth token lacks the `hashpower:read` scope.
 - `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED` (403): This credential cannot access the requested
   account, including when its access has been revoked.
 - `BID_NOT_FOUND` (404): The bid does not exist in this account.

start_time.title: start_time
start_time.description:
Return samples starting with the first interval that starts at or after
 this time. Omit to get the most recent samples, which end with the bid's
 last interval with delivery.

limit.title: limit
limit.description:
Number of samples to return. Defaults to 288; values above 1000 are
 treated as 1000.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.HashrateIn.title: HashrateInterval
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.HashrateIn.description:
Length of one hashrate sample.

 - `HASHRATE_INTERVAL_5M`: 5 minutes.
 - `HASHRATE_INTERVAL_15M`: 15 minutes.
 - `HASHRATE_INTERVAL_1H`: 1 hour.
 - `HASHRATE_INTERVAL_4H`: 4 hours.

purchased_ph.title: purchased_ph
purchased_ph.description: Hashrate bought and validated by Hashpower.

accepted_ph.title: accepted_ph
accepted_ph.description: Hashrate accepted by the destination pool.

rejected_ph.title: rejected_ph
rejected_ph.description: Hashrate rejected by the destination pool.

braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.HashrateSa.title: HashrateSample
braiins.hashpower.delivery.v2.HashrateSa.description:
Average hashrate during one interval, computed from the shares delivered
 and the full interval length. The newest interval may still be in progress
 and a bid's first interval may start before the bid, so those samples read
 lower than the hashrate delivered while they were open.

hashrate_matched_ph.title: hashrate_matched_ph
hashrate_matched_ph.description: Hashrate being sold at this level, estimated over 10 minutes.

hashrate_available_ph.title: hashrate_available_ph
hashrate_available_ph.description: Hashrate offered at this level, estimated over 10 minutes.

amount_sat.title: amount_sat
amount_sat.description: Unspent budget of the bids at this level, in satoshis.

hashrate_matched_ph.title: hashrate_matched_ph
hashrate_matched_ph.description: Hashrate the bids at this level are buying, estimated over 10 minutes.

speed_limit_ph.title: speed_limit_ph
speed_limit_ph.description:
Sum of the speed limits of the bids at this level; a bid limited because of
 delivery problems counts at its reduced limit, which can be 0. Absent when a
 bid at this level has no speed limit, and when the limit is not known, as
 can happen for a moment while the order book changes.

interval.title: interval
interval.description: Length of the interval each summary covers.

limit.title: limit
limit.description:
Maximum number of summaries. Defaults to 100; values above 1000 are
 treated as 1000. The summaries end at the interval of the most recent trade
 and start no earlier than the first trade in the last 2 × `limit` intervals
 before now, at most 30 days back, so a quiet market returns fewer.

ohlc.title: ohlc
ohlc.description: Summaries, oldest first. The last interval may still be open.

limit.title: limit
limit.description:
Number of trades to return. Defaults to 100; values above 1000 are treated
 as 1000.

best_bid_price_sat.title: best_bid_price_sat
best_bid_price_sat.description: Highest bid price. Absent when there are no bids.

best_ask_price_sat.title: best_ask_price_sat
best_ask_price_sat.description: Lowest ask price. Absent when there are no asks.

last_price_sat.title: last_price_sat
last_price_sat.description:
Price of the most recent trade, however long ago: the `price_sat` of the
 newest trade from `ListTrades`. Absent when no trade is known, which is
 also the case for a while after a Hashpower restart, until the next trade.

volume_24h_eh_day.title: volume_24h_eh_day
volume_24h_eh_day.description:
Volume traded during the last 24 hours, in EH·day. Cached for up to 10
 minutes.

hashrate_matched_ph.title: hashrate_matched_ph
hashrate_matched_ph.description: Hashrate being bought, estimated over the last 10 minutes.

hashrate_available_ph.title: hashrate_available_ph
hashrate_available_ph.description: Hashrate offered by sellers, estimated over the last 10 minutes.

as_of.title: as_of
as_of.description:
When Hashpower published the order book the best prices and hashrates come
 from, at most 20 seconds before the call.

braiins.hashpower.market.v2.MarketStatus.title: MarketStatus
braiins.hashpower.market.v2.MarketStatus.description:
Trading status of the market.

 - `MARKET_STATUS_OPEN`: The market is matching orders.
 - `MARKET_STATUS_HALTED`: Matching is suspended.

braiins.hashpower.market.v2.Ohlc.title: Ohlc
braiins.hashpower.market.v2.Ohlc.description:
Price summary (open, high, low, close) for one interval. An interval without
 trades has a volume of 0, and all its prices equal the previous close.

braiins.hashpower.market.v2.OhlcInterval.title: OhlcInterval
braiins.hashpower.market.v2.OhlcInterval.description:
Length of the interval one OHLC summary covers.

 - `OHLC_INTERVAL_5M`: 5 minutes.
 - `OHLC_INTERVAL_15M`: 15 minutes.
 - `OHLC_INTERVAL_1H`: 1 hour.
 - `OHLC_INTERVAL_4H`: 4 hours.
 - `OHLC_INTERVAL_1D`: 1 day.

as_of.title: as_of
as_of.description:
When Hashpower published this order book, at most 20 seconds before the
 call.

braiins.hashpower.market.v2.OrderBook.title: OrderBook
braiins.hashpower.market.v2.OrderBook.description: Order book aggregated by price level.

braiins.hashpower.market.v2.Trade.title: Trade
braiins.hashpower.market.v2.Trade.description: Hashrate matched between bids and asks.

braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolCheckFail.title: PoolCheckFailure
braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolCheckFail.description:
Why a pool check did not succeed. Each value belongs to the `PoolCheckResult` in parentheses.
 New values may be added; handle an unknown value by `result`.

 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_DNS_UNRESOLVED` (`UNREACHABLE`): The pool's host name could not be
   resolved.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_TIMEOUT` (`UNREACHABLE`): The pool did not complete the check in time.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_CONNECT_FAILED` (`UNREACHABLE`): None of the pool's addresses accepted a
   connection.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_CONNECTION_CLOSED` (`UNREACHABLE`): The pool closed or dropped the
   connection during the Stratum handshake.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_PROTOCOL_ERROR` (`UNREACHABLE`): The pool did not follow the Stratum V1
   protocol, for example it sent malformed or oversized messages.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_SUBSCRIBE_UNSUPPORTED` (`INCOMPATIBLE`): The pool's `mining.subscribe`
   response has no extranonce2 size.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_EXTRANONCE2_TOO_SMALL` (`INCOMPATIBLE`): The pool's extranonce2 size is
   smaller than Hashpower needs.
 - `POOL_CHECK_FAILURE_AUTHORIZATION_REJECTED` (`UNAUTHORIZED`): The pool rejected the worker in
   `mining.authorize`.

braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolCheckResu.title: PoolCheckResult
braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolCheckResu.description:
Outcome of a pool check. Unless the result is `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_OK`, `failure` says why;
 on `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_OK` it is absent.

 - `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_OK`: The pool accepted a test Stratum V1 connection and worker from
   Hashpower. Pools that are not `stratum+tcp` are not contacted and carry the
   `POOL_WARNING_CODE_NOT_CHECKED` warning.
 - `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_UNREACHABLE`: The pool did not respond or did not complete the Stratum
   handshake.
 - `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_UNAUTHORIZED`: The pool rejected the worker.
 - `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_INCOMPATIBLE`: The pool's stratum settings are not supported by Hashpower.

braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolErrorReas.title: PoolErrorReason
braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolErrorReas.description:
Values of `google.rpc.ErrorInfo.reason` returned by `PoolService`. The error
 domain is `hashpower.braiins.com`. New reasons may be added; handle unknown
 reasons by their gRPC/HTTP status.

 - `UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL` (401/403): Hashpower could not verify or accept
   the request's authentication. Invalid API keys and keys for another product
   are rejected with HTTP 401 at the gateway, without an `ErrorInfo.reason`.
 - `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` (403): The OAuth token lacks the `hashpower:read` scope.
 - `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED` (403): The credential has no Hashpower account it can view.
 - `INVALID_POOL_URL` (400): The pool URL is malformed or points to an address Hashpower does not
   connect to.

message.title: message
message.description: Explanation of the problem. Human-readable; the text may change.

braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolWarning.title: PoolWarning
braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolWarning.description: A problem that does not prevent delivery.

braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolWarningCo.title: PoolWarningCode
braiins.hashpower.pools.v2.PoolWarningCo.description:
Kind of a `PoolWarning`. New values may be added; show `message` for an unknown value.

 - `POOL_WARNING_CODE_DIFFICULTY_UNKNOWN`: The pool set no share difficulty during the check
   (`difficulty` is absent), so it could not be compared with the recommended minimum.
 - `POOL_WARNING_CODE_DIFFICULTY_BELOW_MINIMUM`: The pool's share difficulty (`difficulty`) is
   below the recommended minimum of 8000.
 - `POOL_WARNING_CODE_NOT_CHECKED`: Hashpower checks only `stratum+tcp` pools. This pool was not
   contacted; the result covers the URL and worker format and, if the host resolved, that it
   has a public address.

pool_url.title: pool_url
pool_url.description:
Pool URL: `[scheme://]host[:port][/key]`. The scheme is `stratum+tcp`
 (the default), `stratum+tcp+secure`, `stratum2+tcp` or
 `stratum2+tcp+insecure`. The host is a DNS name or a public IPv4 address.
 Without a port, Stratum V1 schemes use 3333 and Stratum V2 schemes 3336.
 `stratum+tcp+secure` and `stratum2+tcp` need the pool's authority public
 key as the path; the other schemes take no path. For example
 `stratum+tcp://stratum.braiins.com:3333`.

worker.title: worker
worker.description:
Worker name the pool credits: 1 to 255 bytes, without whitespace or
 control characters. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.

failure.title: failure
failure.description:
Why the check did not succeed. Absent when `result` is
 `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_OK`, set otherwise.

normalized_pool_url.title: normalized_pool_url
normalized_pool_url.description: Canonical form of the pool URL. Use it when placing a bid.

difficulty.title: difficulty
difficulty.description:
Share difficulty the pool set during the check. Absent when the pool set
 none, was not contacted, or was unreachable.

warnings.title: warnings
warnings.description: Problems that do not prevent delivery.

message.title: message
message.description: Explanation of the result. Human-readable; the text may change.

account_id.title: account_id

update_time.title: update_time
update_time.description:
When the bid last changed: an edit of its terms or memo, a cancellation
 request by its owner, or a change of its `degradation`. Pauses and
 cancellations by Hashpower do not change it. Until the first change, the
 time the bid was placed.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Bid.title: Bid
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Bid.description:
A spot market bid. Prices are in satoshis per EH/day; amounts are in
 satoshis; hashrates are in PH/s.

amount_consumed_sat.title: amount_consumed_sat
amount_consumed_sat.description: Budget spent on hashrate, including fees.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.BidProgress.title: BidProgress
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.BidProgress.description: Money a bid has spent, in satoshis.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.BidState.title: BidState
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.BidState.description:
Lifecycle state of a bid. New states may be added; treat unknown values as
 "not finished".

 - `BID_STATE_CREATED`: Accepted by the market but not yet matching.
 - `BID_STATE_ACTIVE`: Matching and buying hashrate.
 - `BID_STATE_PAUSED`: Temporarily not buying hashrate; see `pause_reason`.
 - `BID_STATE_FROZEN`: Stopped by Braiins; contact support.
 - `BID_STATE_CANCELING`: Cancellation requested and in progress.
 - `BID_STATE_CANCELED`: Cancelled. Final state.
 - `BID_STATE_FULFILLED`: Budget fully spent. Final state.
 - `BID_STATE_CREATING`: Returned only by `PlaceBid`: the market accepted the
   bid, but it cannot be read yet. The bid has its `bid_id`, the requested
   destination, price, budget, speed limit and memo, and
   `amount_remaining_sat` equal to the budget. `fee_rate_pct`, `settled`,
   `estimated`, `create_time` and `update_time` are absent, and
   `progress_pct` and `avg_speed_ph` are 0. `GetBid` returns the bid within
   seconds, usually as `BID_STATE_CREATED`; until then `GetBid`, `UpdateBid`
   and `CancelBid` may answer `BID_NOT_FOUND`.
 - `BID_STATE_UPDATING`: Returned only by `UpdateBid`: the market accepted the
   change, but the bid does not show it yet. The returned bid has the
   requested terms; `GetBid` shows them within seconds with the bid's state,
   unless a later change replaces them first.

request_id.title: request_id
request_id.description:
Idempotency key: a UUID you generate for each change, for example a random
 UUID v4. Reuse it only to retry the same request after a timeout, a 429 or
 5xx response, or `OUTCOME_PENDING`; reusing it with a different body fails
 with `REQUEST_ID_REUSED`.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Degradation.title: Degradation
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Degradation.description: Speed limitation applied while the destination has delivery problems.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.DepositStat.title: DepositStatus
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.DepositStat.description:
Processing state of a deposit. New states may be added; treat unknown values
 as "not credited".

 - `DEPOSIT_STATUS_DETECTED`: Seen on the blockchain; not credited yet.
 - `DEPOSIT_STATUS_CREDITED`: Confirmed and credited to the available funds.
 - `DEPOSIT_STATUS_AML_HOLD`: Held for a compliance review; not credited.
 - `DEPOSIT_STATUS_RETURNED`: Sent back after the review; see `return_tx_id`.
 - `DEPOSIT_STATUS_ORPHANED`: No longer in the main chain, usually after a
   reorganization; not credited. It can be detected again.

pool_url.title: pool_url
pool_url.description:
Pool URL: `[scheme://]host[:port][/key]`. The scheme is `stratum+tcp` (the
 default), `stratum+tcp+secure`, `stratum2+tcp` or `stratum2+tcp+insecure`.
 The host is a DNS name or a public IPv4 address. A host whose last label is
 a number, such as `0x7f000001`, must be a dotted-decimal address, and
 `localhost`, `local`, `internal`, `home.arpa` and the names under them are
 not accepted. Without a port, Stratum V1 schemes use 3333 and Stratum V2
 schemes 3336. `stratum+tcp+secure` and `stratum2+tcp` need the pool's
 authority public key as the path; the other schemes take no path. For
 example `stratum+tcp://stratum.braiins.com:3333`.

worker.title: worker

 control characters. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.

max_amount_sat.description: Largest budget for a bid without a speed limit.

min_limited_amount_sat.title: min_limited_amount_sat
min_limited_amount_sat.description: Smallest budget for a bid with a speed limit.

max_limited_amount_sat.title: max_limited_amount_sat
max_limited_amount_sat.description: Largest budget for a bid with a speed limit.

min_limited_duration.title: min_limited_duration
min_limited_duration.description:
Shortest duration a bid with a speed limit must be able to run at its
 limit and price before its budget is spent.

max_current_bids.title: max_current_bids
max_current_bids.description:
Maximum number of created, active and paused bids per account. Frozen and
 canceling bids, which `ListBids` with `current_only` also returns, do not
 count.

cancel_grace_period.title: cancel_grace_period
cancel_grace_period.description: Minimum bid age before it can be cancelled.

price_decrease_interval.title: price_decrease_interval
price_decrease_interval.description: Minimum time between two price decreases of the same bid.

speed_limit_decrease_interval.title: speed_limit_decrease_interval
speed_limit_decrease_interval.description: Minimum time between two speed-limit decreases of the same bid.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.SpotSetting.title: SpotSettings
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.SpotSetting.description:
Spot market settings: the limits a bid must respect. Prices are in satoshis
 per EH/day; amounts are in satoshis; speed limits are in PH/s. An upper bound
 the market does not limit is reported as the largest value the API accepts:
 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1) for prices and amounts, about 1.8e293 (the
 largest double divided by 10^15, so that the limit is a finite number of H/s)
 for the speed limit and 4294967295 for `max_current_bids`. A lower bound the
 market does not limit is reported as the smallest valid value:
 `tick_size_sat` for the price, 1 for amounts, and 0 for the speed limit and
 every duration.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.TradingErro.title: TradingErrorReason
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.TradingErro.description:
Values of `google.rpc.ErrorInfo.reason` returned by `AccountService` and
 `BidService`. The error domain is `hashpower.braiins.com`. New reasons may be
 added; handle unknown reasons by their gRPC/HTTP status. Except for
 `OUTCOME_PENDING`, retry a failed change with a new `request_id`.

 - `UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL` (401/403): Hashpower could not verify or accept
   the request's authentication. Invalid API keys and keys for another product
   are rejected with HTTP 401 at the gateway, without an `ErrorInfo.reason`.
 - `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` (403): The OAuth token lacks `hashpower:read` for reads or
   `hashpower:write` for bid changes. API-key permissions are checked separately.
 - `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED` (403): This credential cannot access the requested
   account, including when its access has been revoked.
 - `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION` (403): The API key can read its own account but
   cannot change bids. A denied read or lost account access returns
   `ACCOUNT_NOT_GRANTED` instead.
 - `BID_NOT_FOUND` (404): The bid does not exist in this account, or was placed moments ago
   and cannot be read yet (see `BID_STATE_CREATING`).
 - `PRICE_OUT_OF_RANGE` (400): The price is outside the range in `SpotSettings`.
 - `PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK` (400): The price is not a multiple of `SpotSettings.tick_size_sat`.
 - `AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` (400): The budget is outside the range in `SpotSettings`.
 - `SPEED_LIMIT_OUT_OF_RANGE` (400): The speed limit is outside the range in `SpotSettings`.
 - `AMOUNT_DECREASE_NOT_ALLOWED` (400): A budget cannot be lowered.
 - `INVALID_DESTINATION` (400): The destination pool URL or worker breaks the rules of
   `Destination`; the message names the problem.
 - `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` (400): The account's available balance is too low.
 - `TOO_MANY_CURRENT_BIDS` (400): The account already has `SpotSettings.max_current_bids`
   created, active or paused bids.
 - `MARKET_HALTED` (400): The market is halted.
 - `BID_NOT_MODIFIABLE` (400): The bid is in a state that does not allow this change.
 - `CANCEL_GRACE_PERIOD` (400): The bid is younger than the cancel grace period.
 - `DECREASE_TOO_SOON` (400): A price or speed-limit decrease happened too recently.
 - `REQUEST_ID_REUSED` (409): The `request_id` was already used with a different request body.
 - `OUTCOME_PENDING` (503): The outcome of the change is not known. Retry with the same
   `request_id`; the change is never applied twice. While the change is still executing, a
   retry returns its outcome once it is known.
   If retries still return `OUTCOME_PENDING` after a minute, keep the original request
   record. For an update or cancellation, call `GetBid`. If that read fails, handle the read
   error before deciding to resubmit.

   For an update, compare the fields you requested with the returned bid. If they match, no
   further update is needed. Otherwise, if the update is still intended, submit it again with
   a new `request_id`. Do not replay an outdated update after a later change to the bid. The
   new command is subject to normal validation.

   For a cancellation, do not resend if the bid is `BID_STATE_CANCELING`,
   `BID_STATE_CANCELED`, or `BID_STATE_FULFILLED`. Otherwise, if cancellation is still
   intended, submit it again with a new `request_id`, subject to normal validation.

   For a placement, list all bids with `current_only=false`, including terminal bids. Page
   backward until the results cover the first attempt, allowing for clock skew, and compare
   the placement's terms. A unique memo chosen before the first attempt can help correlate a
   placement, but it is not an idempotency key. A missing match does not prove non-execution.
   Hashpower does not guarantee when a placed bid appears in `ListBids`.

   The API does not yet provide conclusive automated placement recovery. Stop automatic
   replacement while the placement's outcome remains unknown. Do not create another placement
   with a new UUID or fall back to v1 solely because the outcome remains unknown.
 - `DURATION_TOO_SHORT` (400): The bid's budget would run out sooner than
   `SpotSettings.min_limited_duration` at its speed limit and price.
 - `BID_NOT_READY` (400): The bid was placed moments ago and cannot be changed yet. Retry
   shortly with a new `request_id`.

transaction_id.title: transaction_id
transaction_id.description:
Movement identifier, for example `T1234`. Movements are listed in the
 order they were booked.

time.title: time
time.description: When the movement took effect. It can be earlier than when it was booked.

bid_id.title: bid_id
bid_id.description:
Bid the movement belongs to, for example `B1234`. Empty for other
 movements.

contract_id.title: contract_id
contract_id.description:
Contract the movement belongs to, for example `C1234`. Empty for other
 movements.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Transaction.title: Transaction
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Transaction.description:
A movement of the account's balance. Amounts are in satoshis.

 `available_change_sat` and `blocked_change_sat` are signed changes of
 `Balance.available_sat` and `Balance.blocked_sat`; their sum is the change
 of `Balance.total_sat`. For example, blocking funds for a bid lowers the
 available funds and raises the blocked funds by the same amount, so the
 total does not change.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Transaction.title: TransactionType
braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.Transaction.description:
What a balance movement was. New types may be added; treat unknown values
 like `TRANSACTION_TYPE_OTHER` and rely on the movement's balance changes.

 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_DEPOSIT`: A deposit was credited to the available funds.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_WITHDRAWAL`: Funds were withdrawn from the available funds.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_BID_FUNDS_BLOCKED`: A bid's budget, or a budget increase, was blocked
   from the available funds.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_BID_FUNDS_RELEASED`: Blocked funds returned to the available funds: the
   unspent budget of a finished bid, or a rejected placement or budget increase.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_BID_SETTLEMENT`: Blocked funds paid for hashrate a bid bought, fees
   included.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_CONTRACT_FUNDS_BLOCKED`: Funds were blocked for a contract.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_CONTRACT_FUNDS_RELEASED`: Funds blocked for a contract returned to the
   available funds.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_CONTRACT_SETTLEMENT`: Blocked funds paid for hashrate a contract
   delivered, at the daily PPS rate.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_CONTRACT_PREMIUM`: Blocked funds paid as the contract's premium over the
   daily PPS rate.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_CONTRACT_CANCELLATION_FEE`: Blocked funds paid as the fee for
   cancelling a contract.
 - `TRANSACTION_TYPE_OTHER`: Any other movement, such as a correction.

braiins.hashpower.trading.v2.UpdateBidRe.description: Request for `UpdateBid`. Omitted fields stay unchanged.

google.protobuf.Any.description:
One error detail. `@type` names its type and decides which other fields
are set: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo` sets `reason`,
`domain` and `metadata`; `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.BadRequest`
sets `field_violations`.

reason.description:
`ErrorInfo`: the error reason, a value of `TradingErrorReason`,
`DeliveryErrorReason` or `PoolErrorReason`.

google.protobuf.Duration.description: A signed duration in seconds, with up to nine fractional digits and an `s` suffix (for example, `3s` or `-0.001s`).

google.protobuf.Timestamp.description: A point in time in RFC 3339 format, with up to nanosecond precision. Output uses UTC (`Z`); input may use an offset from UTC.

code.description:
gRPC status code, for example 3 (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`) or 9
(`FAILED_PRECONDITION`). The HTTP status follows from it.

message.description: Developer-facing explanation. The text may change; do not parse it.

braiins_api_key.description:
Account owners create API keys on the account page in Braiins ID.
A key acts only on its own account. Reading requires the Viewer or
Admin role; placing, updating and cancelling bids requires Admin.

 `AccountService` methods and the `BidService` reads.
 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.

Every change of the balance is listed: credited deposits, withdrawals,
 funds blocked for and released from bids, bid settlements, and contract
 movements. Each movement states how it changed the available and blocked
 funds reported by `GetBalance`. Use `bid_id` to list one bid's movements.
 Deposits that are not credited yet are in `ListOnChainTransactions`.

post.summary: Checks a pool and worker before you place a bid on them.
post.description:
`PlaceBid` accepts every pool URL and worker this method accepts, in the
 same canonical form. For a `stratum+tcp` pool, Hashpower opens a Stratum
 V1 connection and tries to authorize the worker, which completes within 15
 seconds; set a client timeout of at least 20 seconds. Pools with other
 schemes are not contacted: the result is `POOL_CHECK_RESULT_OK` with the
 `POOL_WARNING_CODE_NOT_CHECKED` warning. Whatever the scheme, a host whose
 DNS answers are all non-public addresses fails with `INVALID_POOL_URL`;
 `PlaceBid` does not resolve the host. Use `normalized_pool_url` from the
 response when placing a bid. The check names no account, but your credential
 must still allow you to view at least one Hashpower account. An API key
 checks only the account it belongs to.

 Error reasons: `INVALID_POOL_URL` (400), and those of the 401 and 403
 responses.

 OAuth requires `hashpower:read`; API keys require read access.

 Rate limit: burst of 3, then 6 per minute per client IP.

get.summary:
Lists the account's bids, newest first: by creation time, then by bid ID.
 Each page continues after the last bid of the previous one, so bids placed
 or finished while you page neither repeat nor shift the others.

 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.

post.summary: Places a new bid and returns it.
post.description:
The bid delivers to the destination in canonical form, the form
 `PoolService.ValidatePool` returns as `normalized_pool_url`. Every
 destination `ValidatePool` accepts is accepted here; `ValidatePool` also
 rejects a host whose addresses are all non-public, which this method does
 not resolve. The bid's funds are blocked from the account's available
 balance. Fails with `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` when the available balance is too
 low. A bid that cannot be read yet is returned as `BID_STATE_CREATING`.

 Error reasons: `PRICE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK`,
 `AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `SPEED_LIMIT_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `DURATION_TOO_SHORT`,
 `INVALID_DESTINATION`, `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, `TOO_MANY_CURRENT_BIDS` and
 `MARKET_HALTED` (400), `REQUEST_ID_REUSED` (409), `OUTCOME_PENDING` (503),
 and those of the 401 and 403 responses.

 Rate limit: burst of 10, then 30 per minute per client IP, shared by
 `PlaceBid`, `UpdateBid` and `CancelBid`.
 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:write` scope or an API key allowed to change bids.

patch.summary: Changes a bid's price, budget, speed limit or memo and returns the bid.
patch.description:
Only the fields present in the request change. The returned bid has the
 new terms; it is `BID_STATE_UPDATING` while the bid does not show them yet.
 A retry after a later change to the bid, or after the bid finished, returns
 the bid as it is, because it will not show this change again.

 A price decrease and a speed-limit decrease are each allowed once per
 `price_decrease_interval` and `speed_limit_decrease_interval`.

 Right after `PlaceBid`, while `GetBid` still answers `BID_NOT_FOUND` for
 the new bid, this method fails with `BID_NOT_FOUND` too. Retry shortly
 with a new `request_id`.

 Price, budget and speed-limit increases are allowed. Use a speed limit
 of 0 to remove it. Budget decreases are not allowed.

 Error reasons: `PRICE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK`,
 `AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `SPEED_LIMIT_OUT_OF_RANGE`,
 `AMOUNT_DECREASE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `DURATION_TOO_SHORT`, `BID_NOT_MODIFIABLE`,
 `DECREASE_TOO_SOON`, `MARKET_HALTED` and `BID_NOT_READY` (400),
 `BID_NOT_FOUND` (404),
 `REQUEST_ID_REUSED` (409), `OUTCOME_PENDING` (503), and those of the 401
 and 403 responses.

 Rate limit: burst of 10, then 30 per minute per client IP, shared by
 `PlaceBid`, `UpdateBid` and `CancelBid`.
 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:write` scope or an API key allowed to change bids.

get.summary:
Returns the best share of a bid: the recorded best share with the highest
 difficulty attributed by destination and bid lifetime, including the
 one-minute grace period after the bid ends.
get.description:
A bid placed moments ago can be `BID_NOT_FOUND` for a short while.

 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.

 Rate limit: burst of 60, then 120 per minute per client IP, shared by all
 `DeliveryService` methods.

get.summary: Returns a bid's delivered hashrate per interval, oldest first.
get.description:
Samples cover the intervals from the bid's first to its last delivery;
 intervals in between without delivery read 0. Intervals after the last
 delivery are not returned, so for a bid that stopped buying, for example a
 paused one, the newest sample is not its current hashrate: compare the
 sample's `start_time` with now. A bid without delivery yet has no samples,
 and a bid placed moments ago can be `BID_NOT_FOUND` for a short while.

 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:read` scope or an API key with read access.

 Rate limit: burst of 60, then 120 per minute per client IP, shared by all
 `DeliveryService` methods.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description:
Return samples starting with the first interval that starts at or after
 this time. Omit to get the most recent samples, which end with the bid's
 last interval with delivery.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Number of samples to return. Defaults to 288; values above 1000 are
 treated as 1000.

post.summary: Cancels a bid and returns it.
post.description:
Cancellation is asynchronous: the returned bid is usually in
 `BID_STATE_CANCELING`. Its unspent budget is released when it reaches
 `BID_STATE_CANCELED`. Fails with `CANCEL_GRACE_PERIOD` when the bid is
 younger than the market's cancel grace period.

 Right after `PlaceBid`, while `GetBid` still answers `BID_NOT_FOUND` for
 the new bid, this method fails with `BID_NOT_FOUND` too. Retry shortly
 with a new `request_id`.

 Error reasons: `BID_NOT_MODIFIABLE` and `CANCEL_GRACE_PERIOD` (400),
 `BID_NOT_FOUND` (404), `REQUEST_ID_REUSED` (409), `OUTCOME_PENDING` (503),
 and those of the 401 and 403 responses.

 Rate limit: burst of 10, then 30 per minute per client IP, shared by
 `PlaceBid`, `UpdateBid` and `CancelBid`.
 Requires the OAuth `hashpower:write` scope or an API key allowed to change bids.

get.summary:
Lists the most recent OHLC price summaries (open, high, low, close), one
 per interval, oldest first.
get.description:
Summaries are cached for up to 60 seconds, so a trade can take up to a
 minute to appear in them.

 Rate limit: burst of 30, then 60 per minute per client IP, shared by all
 `MarketService` methods.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Length of the interval each summary covers.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of summaries. Defaults to 100; values above 1000 are
 treated as 1000. The summaries end at the interval of the most recent trade
 and start no earlier than the first trade in the last 2 × `limit` intervals
 before now, at most 30 days back, so a quiet market returns fewer.

get.summary: Returns the current order book, aggregated by price level.
get.description:
Fails with 503 while no current order book is available, for example
 shortly after a Hashpower restart.

 Rate limit: burst of 30, then 60 per minute per client IP, shared by all
 `MarketService` methods.

 account's fee rate is returned by `GetSpotFees`. No authentication is
 required.
